newsitem.title: UK: Huntingdon sure can meet UK govt demands.
newsitem.headline: Huntingdon sure can meet UK govt demands.

text.p: Huntingdon Life Sciences Group Plc, the animal testing company whose shares were suspended last week, said on Thursday it was confident of completing changes demanded by government of practices relating to its treatment of animals.
"Huntingdon is confident that it can complete all the necessary changes now set out by the Home Office in their notification," said the group in a statement attached to its half-year results.
The group said in the next few weeks it would seek Home Office authorisation of those changes and apply for certificates for each of its research centres.

The government revoked the group's licence to conduct experiments on animals last week and Home Office junior minister George Howarth warned the move could shut the company down, with the loss of 1,400 jobs.
Howarth said if the company remedied "extremely serious" failures and omissions at its plant the government would be prepared to consider an application for a replacement certificate.

The company announced a loss after tax of 308,000 stg in the six months ended June 30, 1997, after exceptional costs which included 1.097 million stg for advisers' fees and expenses arising from Huntingdon's response to allegations from animal rights groups.
The group made a profit of 1.989 million stg in the six months ended June 30, 1996.
